newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end with pared gains.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end with pared gains.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed with pared gains after selling developed during the latter half of the session, traders said.
The selling was prompted by a sharp drop in U.S. stock markets and lower bond markets, they noted.
Lumber mills, apparently interpreting the lower stocks and bonds as bearish economic signals, began selling lumber futures. The selling was thought to be hedging future production.
Trade reports of higher cash lumber prices this week produced local and fund buying early. But, that buying eased near midsession and the gains were erased by the late selling.
Lumber closed up $2.70 to down $2.00 with November up the most at $364.10 per thousand board feet. November peaked Wednesday at $371.50.
